I attached "redlines_orderform_v1.docx" that highlights the MSA/Order Form changes. High level: we want to add a short timebox for on-prem/inspection requests, clarify ephemeral staging access for pen tests, and a scoped list of artifacts we will deliver for SOC 2 status checks.

1) Can you confirm who on ClearWell should receive the SOC2 snapshot and who will own scheduling the pen test?
2) If Q3 works, suggest we hold a 30-minute sync (legal + security) next week to walk the redlines so counsel only needs to review the final packet.

If helpful I can also route a short mutual action plan doc to your procurement contact.

Subject: Re: Order form redlines + security exhibit — evidence cadence & pen-test window

Alyssa — thanks for the quick reply. A few technical clarifications from our side to streamline legal language: 

1) Scope of data for pen test: Redwood's recommended pattern is that pen tests target a staging environment that is logically isolated and seeded with synthetic PII where possible. For production-slice tests we require a documented runbook and a max 4-hour blast window unless otherwise agreed.

2) Ephemeral access model: we can support ephemeral SSH/console access for a 48-hour window per scheduled test; we prefer that be scoped to specific IPs and timebox language be added to the exhibit.

3) SOC 2 artifacts: we'll provide a redacted SOC2 snapshot and a checklist of the artifacts included. I've attached a SOC2-snapshot.pdf and a pen-test-window.xlsx with the proposed Q3 windows (week-of Jul 19, Aug 9, Sep 13).

For legal redlines: if ClearWell accepts a 30-day evidence-response SLA (i.e., Redwood will respond to evidence requests within 30 days and flag any items requiring follow-up), we can add that as an operational clause rather than a blanket right to inspect. That typically helps legal teams avoid open-ended inspection rights while preserving the assurance you need.

Happy to walk through the technical bits on the call.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachments: SOC2-snapshot.pdf, pen-test-window.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + security exhibit — evidence cadence & pen-test window

Alyssa / team —

Following Karthik's technical notes, legal is recommending the following compromise language to close most open items quickly: 

- Limited inspection right: Redwood will accept an inspection clause narrowly scoped to: (a) on-site or remote inspection on a mutually agreed 30-day notice window; (b) limited to the artifacts enumerated in the Security Exhibit; (c) Redwood to redact customer-sensitive telemetry where applicable.
- Evidence SLA: Redwood to provide SOC2 snapshot and listed artifacts within 30 days of a written request; if additional artifacts are required we will follow a short escalation path (security contact -> legal) to scope them.
- Pen test: Redwood will permit pen testing against a staging environment under an ephemeral access model with a signed statement of work from procurement naming the vendor and confirming the test dates.

If ClearWell is comfortable with that approach, we'll incorporate the exact wording into the exhibit and provide a redline for your counsel to review. I dropped a short mutual action plan in Drive to reduce back-and-forth: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB_Redlines-MAP

Marissa — can you please confirm you'd like legal to produce the exhibit redline and I'll route it through our platform counsel this week?

Thanks,
